Marcus John Whitehead

Anaesthetist
Not specified

Anaesthesia Type
Spinal anaesthesia

Procedure
Total left hip replacement Posterolateral approach to the left hip - Surgical site closed in layers - Skin closed with subcuticular sutures - Covered with sterile dresskng

Diagnosis
End-stage OA of the left hip

Findings
- Severe degenerative changes in the left hip joint noted, with significant cartilage loss
- Noevidence of infection or abnormal surrounding tissue

Tissue Removed
Left femoral head

Prostheses or Implants
Cemeented prosthetic implant placed in the L hip

Estimated Blood Loss
Approximately 150 mL

Complications
No intraoperative complications

Post-Operative Care
- Enoxaparin 40 mg SC once daily for thromboprophylaxis
- Early mobilisation with physio to commence later today
- Regular paracetamol 1g every 6h for postoperative pain management

Plan
- Send the removed femoral head for histological examination
- Monitor for signs of infection, VTE, or other complications

General anaesthesia

- Significant cartilage erosion
- Osteophyte formation consistent with end-stage OA

- Severely eroded cartilage
- Osteophytes from the R knee joint

Cemented total knee prosthesis

Minimal

None

- Initiated post-op analgesia with morphine 10mg via PCA pump
- Antibiotic prophylaxis with cefuroxime 1.5g IV for 24h post-op

Plan
- Monitor for signs of infection or thrombosis
- Encourage mobilisation with physiotherapy as per post-op protocol
- Continue routine post-op care and pain management as required

event_text:
Ethel Joanne Duffy

Anaesthesia Type
GA

Procedure
Total left hip replacement

Incision
Posterolateral approach to the left hip

Diagnosis
End-stag OA of the left hip

Findings
- Severe cartilage degeneration noted in the acetabulum and femoral head
- Surrounding soft tissues appeared unremarkable with no evidece of acute inflammation or infection

Tissue Removed
- Degenerated femoral head of the left hip
- Damaged cartilage from the acetabular surface

Prostheses or Implants
- Cemented acetabular cup
- Cemented femoral stem with amodular head

Closure Technique
- Layers closed using absorbable wsutures for deep tissue
- Skin closed with staples
- Sterile dressing applied

Estimated Blood Loss
250 mL

Complications
None

Post-Operative Care
- Prophylactic enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously once daily for 4 weeks to reduce risk of DVT
- Oral oxycodone 5 mg every 4â€“6 hours as needed for pain control
- No further doses of IV cefuroxime required after intraoperative admiinistration

Plan
- Encourage mobilisation with physio startnig on postoperative day 1
- Monitor for signs of infection or thromboembolic events
- Reassess pain management requirements daily
- Send removed tissue (degenerative femoral head and damaged cartilage) for histopathology

Additional Notes
- Consultant oversight provided by Dr.
